content_units: Uneven Cooling Snapshot

Your symptoms point first to   airflow/distribution problems  , then   solar heat load on the bedroom  , and only after that to   refrigerant or performance faults  . With a   6-year-old split system  , a repair is often still worth trying if the fix stays under your   AUD 400   limit.
Priority Troubleshooting Checklist
Step   Action   What to Check   Expected Result
1   Confirm mode and setpoint   Cooling mode, fan speed on High/Auto, set temp around 22-24°C   Strong steady cool airflow
2   Check airflow path   Bedroom door open, no furniture/curtains blocking return or supply air path   Better air movement to bedroom
3   Compare room heat gain   Afternoon sun on bedroom windows/walls, blinds/curtains quality, warm glass or walls   If bedroom heats faster, load imbalance is likely
4   Inspect indoor airflow   Weak airflow at head unit, unusual noise, icing, damp smell, louvers not sweeping properly   Normal airflow without frost or odor
5   Check outdoor unit condition   Outdoor coil dirty, unit in harsh western sun, blocked clearance, fan running properly   Outdoor unit rejects heat efficiently
6   Measure performance gap   After 20-30 min of cooling, compare living room vs bedroom temperature and vent air feel   Helps confirm distribution vs capacity issue
7   Book service if still uneven   Ask for coil clean, temperature split test, fan/capacitor check, refrigerant check   Clear diagnosis before spending more
Most Likely Causes in Your Case
1) Air distribution imbalance
- Most common with a single split head serving an open living area while a bedroom sits farther away.
- The living room cools first because it gets the direct supply air.
- The bedroom stays warm if there is poor circulation, a closed door, or no good return-air path.
2) High afternoon heat load in the bedroom
- Your note that it is   worse on hot afternoons   strongly suggests solar gain.
- West-facing windows, unshaded glass, warm roof space, or poor insulation can overwhelm the bedroom.
- In this case, the AC may be working reasonably, but the room is gaining heat faster than it can be cooled.
3) Dirty outdoor coil or restricted condenser airflow
- Even if the indoor filter was cleaned last month, the   outdoor unit   may still be dirty.
- A clogged condenser reduces cooling performance, especially on very hot Brisbane afternoons.
- This often shows up as “works okay in the morning, struggles later.”
4) Low refrigerant or minor refrigeration fault
- Possible if cooling is weaker than it used to be across the whole apartment.
- More likely if the unit runs for long periods without reaching set temperature.
- Can also cause coil icing or reduced cooling during peak heat.
5) Fan, capacitor, sensor, or louver issue
- If indoor fan speed is lower than expected, air does not throw far enough.
- A faulty thermistor may make the unit think the area is cool because the living room near the head unit cools quickly.
- Stuck louvers can dump cold air into one zone instead of circulating it.
What You Can Try Before Spending Money
Option 1: Improve bedroom air movement   Open bedroom door, run fan to pull cool air from living room into bedroom, keep indoor fan on High   Low-cost test
Try airflow fix
Option 2: Cut afternoon bedroom heat gain   Close blockout curtains/blinds before noon, reduce west sun, limit internal heat sources   Often the biggest comfort improvement
Reduce heat gain
Option 3: Check outdoor unit surroundings   Clear leaves/debris, keep airflow space around condenser, look for heavy dirt buildup   Helps in hot weather
Outdoor unit guide
Option 4: Book a service call with a spend cap   Ask for diagnosis and quote first, with authorization only up to AUD 400   Best next step if simple fixes fail
Book service
What a Technician Would Inspect
-   Temperature split   across the indoor unit: whether supply air is sufficiently colder than room air.
-   Indoor coil and blower wheel  : hidden dirt can reduce airflow even when the filter looks fine.
-   Outdoor coil cleanliness   and condenser fan operation.
-   Refrigerant pressures   and signs of leakage.
-   Compressor current draw   and capacitor condition.
-   Thermistor/sensor readings   and whether the unit is cycling correctly.
-   Louver swing and air throw   direction.
-   Drain and icing signs   that suggest restricted airflow or gas issues.
-   System sizing vs apartment layout  : 82 m² can be challenging for one split if the bedroom is isolated or sun-exposed.
When Repair May Not Be Worth It
Repair starts to look poor value if you see one or more of these:
- The quoted fix is   above AUD 400   and does not clearly solve the uneven-room problem.
- The technician says the unit is   undersized for the layout  , not actually broken.
- There is a   refrigerant leak in coil/pipework   that is costly to locate and repair.
- The   compressor   is failing or noisy; compressor-related work often exceeds your budget.
- The unit still cools unevenly after cleaning/service because the real issue is   apartment layout or bedroom heat load  .
- You get repeated callouts for different parts within a short period.

A practical rule: if the quote is near your budget and the cause is only coil cleaning, fan capacitor, sensor, or minor service work, repair is usually worth it. If it involves compressor, major leak repair, or fundamental sizing/distribution limits, saving toward a second bedroom unit or replacement is usually smarter.
